extracted.intended_audience: immigration practitioners, DHS/USCIS adjudicators, consular officers, visa applicants, and public commenters/stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and adjudicative criteria for determining whether an alien is inadmissible as a public charge when applying for admission, adjustment of status, extension of stay, or change of status under the proposed DHS public charge rule. Covers applicability, required attestations/evidence, category-specific applicability, and procedural screening by DOS/USCIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to applicants for admission and adjustment of status
rubrics_metrics.description: This rule would apply to any alien subject to section 212(a)(4) of the Act, 8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4), who is applying for admission to the United States or is applying for adjustment of status to that of lawful permanent resident before DHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOS screens applicants subject to public charge inadmissibility grounds and who are seeking nonimmigrant or immigrant visas at consular posts worldwide; many immigrants obtain visas at consular posts prior to port-of-entry admission. (See proposed 8 CFR 212.20 and accompanying discussion.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailoring of public-charge processes to the benefit sought
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the processes, evidentiary requirements, and nature of the stay in the United States for aliens seeking a visa, admission, extension of stay, change of status, and adjustment of status differ, DHS proposes public charge processes appropriately tailored to the benefit the alien seeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjudicators should vary process and evidentiary requirements depending on whether the alien seeks admission, adjustment, extension, or change of status; e.g., adjustment of status applicants undergo a different process than a temporary visitor from Canada.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of type and duration of nonimmigrant stay
rubrics_metrics.description: The type of nonimmigrant status and the duration of the nonimmigrant’s stay in the United States would be considered in assessing whether the applicant has met his or her burden of demonstrating that he or she is likely to become a public charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-term, temporary visits (e.g., a B-2 one-week vacation) weigh differently because the individual likely only needs resources to cover short-term expenses; frequency and expected length of stay are relevant factors for the public-charge assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection/port-of-entry inadmissibility determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for admission are inspected at, or when encountered between, ports of entry. They are inspected by immigration officers to assess, among other things, whether they are inadmissible under section 212(a) of the Act, including section 212(a)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspection officers make public-charge inadmissibility determinations at ports of entry; DOS makes related determinations during consular visa processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's burden to demonstrate not likely to become a public charge; mandatory factors including affidavits of support
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether the applicant has demonstrated that he or she is not inadmissible on the public charge ground, DOS reviews all of the mandatory factors, including any required affidavits of support submitted under section 213A of the Act, 8 U.S.C. 1183a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits of support and the mandatory factors listed in statute/regulation are central pieces of evidence; DOS/USCIS will review these as part of the admissibility determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOS consular screening and likely change to visa-issuance guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: This process would not change under the proposed rule, but it is likely that DOS will amend its guidance to prevent the issuance of visas to inadmissible aliens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOS would continue to review affidavits of support and screen aliens for public charge inadmissibility in accordance with applicable regulations and instructions prior to the alien undergoing inspection and applying for admission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lawful permanent residents treated as applicants for admission in limited circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Although lawful permanent residents generally are not considered to be applicants for admission upon their return from a trip abroad, in certain limited circumstances a lawful permanent resident will be considered an applicant for admission and, therefore, subject to an inadmissibility determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circumstances include abandonment/relinquishment of status; continuous absence >180 days; post-departure illegal activity; departing while under legal process seeking removal/extradition; committing an offense in INA 212(a)(2) unless waived; entering at time/place other than designated. If treated as applicant, public-charge inadmissibility may be applied on return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of public benefits receipt in extension of stay and change of status adjudications
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS is proposing to consider whether the alien has received since obtaining the nonimmigrant status he or she seeks to extend or to which he or she seeks to change, is currently receiving, or is likely to receive public benefits as defined in the proposed rule, when adjudicating an application to extend a nonimmigrant stay or change a nonimmigrant status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although 212(a)(4) by its terms applies to applicants for visas, admission, and adjustment, DHS asserts a government interest in ensuring self-sufficiency for the duration of temporary stays and proposes to apply public-benefits considerations to extensions/changes of status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation requirement under penalty of perjury for extension/change applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS is proposing to require an applicant for an extension of stay or change of status to attest that he or she has neither received since obtaining the nonimmigrant status he or she seeks to extend or to which he or she seeks to change, nor is currently receiving or likely to receive any such public benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must answer questions on their application form under penalty of perjury regarding receipt of public benefits; these responses would be used in determining whether the applicant met his or her burden to establish eligibility for extension of stay or change of status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of maintenance of status, sufficient financial means, and gainful employment
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS would consider whether the applicant has provided evidence of maintenance of status and that he or she has sufficient financial means to maintain the status he or she seeks, or that he or she will be gainfully employed in such status, as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjudicators may evaluate evidence of maintenance of status (e.g., prior compliance), proof of financial resources to maintain the sought status, or employment offers/expected earnings as part of public-charge evaluation for extensions/changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential requirement to submit Form I-944
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the information the alien provides in support of the application for extension of stay or change of status, USCIS would determine whether the applicant should also submit Form I-944 in order to demonstrate that he or she is unlikely to receive public benefits during the temporary stay in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS discretionally may request Form I-944 (public-charge declaration/financial resources) to support findings about likelihood of receiving public benefits during the period of stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status-specific evidentiary examples (medical, student, employment-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: a B-2 nonimmigrant admitted to seek medical treatment and seeking extension must submit evidence that he or she has the financial means to pay for additional medical treatment and otherwise support him/herself; an alien seeking to extend or change to F-1 or M-1 must submit evidence of financial ability to pay for study and to financially support him/herself; employment-based nonimmigrants may submit tax return transcripts, W-2, or other documentation evidencing income from gainful employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations to AFM and 8 CFR provisions cited in the rule illustrate forms of acceptable financial documentation (I-20, SEVIS, tax transcripts, W-2s); evidence should be appropriate to the nonimmigrant status being sought and the anticipated duration of stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of application responses and evidence to determine requirement to file additional forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The responses to questions about receipt of public benefits on extension/change application forms would be used in determining whether the applicant has met his or her burden to establish eligibility and whether additional documentation (e.g., Form I-944) should be requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjudicators should treat the attestations as evidence-bearing responses under penalty of perjury and may require follow-up documentation based on those responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonimmigrant-category-specific applicability (Table 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 4 provides a summary of nonimmigrant categories and the applicability of the public benefit condition to such categories, including whether a category is eligible to apply for extension of stay or change of status (may file Form I-129 or I-539) and whether it is subject to the public benefit condition under proposed 8 CFR 214.1(a)(3)(iv), 214.1(a)(4)(iv); 248.1(c)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjudicators and practitioners should consult the Table 4 entries for per-category determinations (e.g., which classifications are eligible to file extensions/changes and which are subject to the public-benefit condition); the table lists many classifications (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, J, K, L, M, N, NATO classes, CW, etc.) with specific notes (e.g., duration of status exceptions, INA/22 CFR references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to provide information to employer when employer files petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Aliens in nonimmigrant classifications whose employers will be filing Form I-129 or Form I-129CW on their behalf will be required to provide this information to their employer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an employer files on behalf of an alien, the alien must still supply required answers/evidence about public-benefits receipt so the employer can complete the petition; this is a procedural compliance requirement tied to adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy rationale: government interest in self-sufficiency during entire stay
rubrics_metrics.description: The government’s interest in a nonimmigrant alien’s ability to maintain self-sufficiency for the duration of the temporary stay does not end with his or her admission as a nonimmigrant. Aliens therefore should remain self-sufficient for the entire period of their stay, including any extension of stay or additional period of stay afforded by a change of status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS ties this rationale to statutory policy statements (e.g., PRWORA and 8 U.S.C. 1601) to justify considering public-benefits receipt for extensions/changes and to require attestations/evidence of financial ability to remain self-sufficient.
